reason: The arithmetic checks out and I reproduced the Monte Carlo. Score = adj_edge_J + 0.1*div_J (CONTEXT l.10). Pooled div J changes by +1/Den for a TP and by -J/Den for an FP. Public: 0.1/44 = +0.0023 (matches R15DS-1). Private: 0.1/105 = +0.00095, and an FP costs -0.0002..-0.0004. So break-even is J/(1+J) = 0.17-0.29. The ratio lambda/Den is ~0.057-0.059 on both public and private, so the annotation-density factor a cancels in the mean and only widens the sd. My own MC with the stated parameters (N = 400k) gives: w_pub 0 -> -0.00044, P(C>0) .33; w_pub .45 -> +0.00043, sd .0022, P(C>0) .50, p10/p90 -0.0019/+0.0034; w_pub .7 -> +0.0009, P(C>0) .60. These match the finding. Probe 45 is verified in the ledger: 56606948, L (7.49,7.67] h, insertion gate did NOT fire. On feasibility the finding cannot fail: it is quote-only, with no build, no submit and no rung input, and it fits finals clause (9), which already carries the DIV caveat. Its core message survives every alternative I tried: C is near a coin flip, with an sd of ~0.002 that is larger than the mean. Three points need amending, none of them fatal. (1) The lab-like branch Beta(1.5,7) rests on 4 in-sample FP events. The parallel scan R20ID-1 extended the same lab to 29 arms and found cap 6 is a local dip: from cap 8 up to cap 24 + fc2 the in-sample lab rises (+0.0013 vs K2). So 'second lab/public sign flip' holds only for the 4->6 step, not for the cap direction. Two other reasonable priors (pooled evidence Beta(3,6); lab branch Beta(2.5,7)) give C ~+0.0008, P(C>0) ~0.6. (2) 'About 44 extra public insertions' is really 44 public clips, i.e. ~65 insertions at 1.5 per clip (~2.5-3 scorable). This does not change the conclusion. (3) 'Refutes R15DS-7' is too strong for a <15% event seen once; 'contradicts' is the right word. The quote carries real value for the user's 29 Sep pick: it keeps the public +0.002 from being read as a private gain. It is not a closed line in disguise and not a node-count artefact. The mixture weight 0.45 is judgmental, and the quote must say so.
